sect1.title:
#$ #$
HASH_DOLLAR
sect1.para: The #$ module reference identifies the module and package in which the current MACRO or FUNCTIONMACRO was defined. It is useful when a macro imports or references definitions that belong to its defining module, regardless of the module from which the macro is called. This prevents those references from being resolved relative to the call site.
Within a macro, #$ can be used as an import source or as the beginning of a qualified module reference:
The #$ reference also preserves the package context of a macro. The caret can be used to navigate from that context, for example:

Use $ for the current module or folder, and append ^ to a module specifier to navigate to its container. The #$ reference is specifically for retaining the macro's defining module and package context during expansion.
